status_summary: Executive Order 14153 (signed 2025-01-20, published 2025-01-29) directs reinstating the 2019 Coastal Plain environmental impact statement and 2020 record of decision with additional leasing, reinstating the 2020 NPR-A Integrated Activity Plan record of decision and rescinding the 2024 NPR-A rule, reinstating the 2020 Ambler Road record of decision, reinstating the 2020 Alaska Roadless rule, and reinstating Public Land Orders 7899 to 7903; it does not mention Willow. BLM rescinded its 2024 NPR-A management rule (final rule published 2025-11-17, effective 2025-12-17), held an NPR-A lease sale on 2026-03-18, the first since 2019 and the first under Public Law 119-21 (BLM reports $163,696,722 in total receipts from 11 companies on 187 of 625 tracts offered, covering about 1.33 million of roughly 5.5 million acres offered), and held a Coastal Plain sale on 2026-06-05 (BLM reports five of 58 tracts offered, 72,049 acres of about 688,829 offered, drew bids from two companies, Hex Energy LLC and AIDEA, totaling $3,741,528, with about half going to Alaska; BLM says it reversed the 2023 Coastal Plain lease cancellations and issued a new 2025 record of decision since January 2025), and press coverage describes pending litigation over Arctic Refuge leasing; two suits filed in February 2026 challenge the NPR-A sale, and a draft settlement filed in July 2026 in the State of Alaska's and AIDEA's suits over the 2025 Arctic Refuge lease sale would loosen limits on leasing there; no injunction or vacatur was reported in the sources read. BLM proposed NPR-A production site criteria on 2026-09-08, and a presidential decision published 2025-10-08 directed agencies to issue authorizations for the Ambler Road. Whether the 2020 plans and public land orders were actually reinstated, Willow pad approvals and the Tongass roadless action were not verified. Public Law 119-52 (approved 2025-12-11), a Congressional Review Act resolution, provides that BLM's 2024-12-09 Coastal Plain leasing record of decision has no force or effect, which aligns with the Mandate's call to return to the 2020 Arctic Refuge leasing review. The Ninth Circuit on 2026-10-06 dismissed as moot the appeal over the 2023 cancellation of seven AIDEA Coastal Plain leases, vacated the district court decision and remanded for dismissal, noting that Interior reinstated the leases after issuing a new record of decision in October 2025.

timeline.event: Executive Order 14153, Unleashing Alaska's Extraordinary Resource Potential, is published; it directs the Interior Secretary to resume Arctic Refuge Coastal Plain leasing and rescind lease cancellations there, and (per a later USDA notice) to exempt the Tongass National Forest from the 2001 Roadless Rule.
BLM proposes to rescind its May 2024 NPR-A management rule.
A presidential decision on the Ambler Road Project under ANILCA section 1106(a)(2) is published, directing agencies to promptly issue the needed authorizations.
BLM requests nominations and comments for the 2025 NPR-A lease sale, described as the first since 2019 and the first under Public Law 119-21.
BLM publishes its final rule rescinding and replacing the 2024 NPR-A management rule, effective 2025-12-17.

Public Law 119-52 (H.J.Res. 131, 139 Stat. 701) is approved; under the Congressional Review Act it disapproves the Bureau of Land Management's Coastal Plain Oil and Gas Leasing Program Record of Decision of 2024-12-09, which a GAO opinion of 2025-08-25 found to be a rule, and provides that it has no force or effect.
BLM publishes the notice of the 2026 NPR-A oil and gas lease sale: more than 600 tracts, sealed bids due 2026-03-16, bid opening 2026-03-18.

BLM holds the NPR-A lease sale (the first since 2019 and the first under Public Law 119-21) and reports $163,696,722 in total receipts from 11 companies on 187 of the 625 tracts offered, covering about 1,334,967 of roughly 5.5 million acres offered; BLM also states that an updated Integrated Activity Plan reopens nearly 82 percent of the reserve to leasing.
BLM publishes the notice of the 2026 Coastal Plain (Arctic Refuge) oil and gas lease sale, with bid opening set for 2026-06-05.

BLM holds the Coastal Plain (Arctic Refuge) lease sale and reports five of 58 tracts offered (72,049 acres of about 688,829) received bids from two companies, Hex Energy LLC and AIDEA, totaling $3,741,528, with about $2 million going to Alaska; BLM calls it the first successful sale under the 2025 tax law and says it reversed 2023 lease cancellations and issued a new 2025 record of decision since January 2025.
USDA proposes rescinding the national 2001 Roadless Rule; its background notes that Executive Order 14153 directs reinstating the 2020 Alaska Roadless Rule for the Tongass.

The Ninth Circuit (Friedland and De Alba, Circuit Judges, and Lasnik, District Judge, sitting by designation; Nos. 25-3231 and 25-3344, argued 2026-09-15) dismisses as moot the appeal in Alaska Industrial Development and Export Authority v. Department of the Interior concerning the 2023 cancellation of seven Coastal Plain leases, vacates the District of Alaska decision (D.C. No. 3:24-cv-00051-SLG) and remands with instructions to dismiss, because Interior issued a new record of decision in October 2025 and reinstated the leases; the memorandum is unpublished.
